I am 55 years old and have farmed this land for 35 years. I never went to school, but I know my 10 mu like the back of my hand. My husband and I are the only ones living here now — our children work in the factory in town and send some money home, but we still need the farm to live. With just two of us and some off-farm work, I have to be careful with labor. I cannot manage too much cotton because it needs picking four or five times and spraying every few days when the bollworms come. So I divide my land the same way as last year: about 7 mu for wheat and maize, and a little over 3 mu for cotton. The wheat-maize rotation is my anchor — it gives us grain to eat and some cash to buy other things.

For the wheat, I will rotary till in mid-October and sow the improved seed I buy from the village shop. I learned long ago that saving my own seed does not grow well for wheat. I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — about 50 kg — and if the wheat looks yellow at jointing time, I throw down another half bag of urea. That is what my neighbors do and it works. I irrigate three times: before winter, at jointing, and at flowering. The well water costs money for pumping, but dry wheat means no harvest, so I do not skip it. I spray herbicide once in early spring and insecticide twice. I expect about 1000 jin per mu if the weather is normal.

For the summer maize, there is no time to rest after wheat harvest in early June — we plant within a few days, no-tillage, directly into the stubble. There is no time to plow; the season is too short. Maize must be hybrid seed or it will not yield. I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer in the planting holes. Maize only needs one or two irrigations in summer, depending on rain. If July is wet, maybe only once at the big trumpet stage. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice. If the weather holds, I expect about 1100 jin per mu.

For cotton, I rotary till in late April and plant improved seed. I use one bag of compound per mu as base fertilizer, and a little urea later when the plants are growing. Cotton needs two irrigations, but the real work is the spraying — bollworms come every year without fail, and aphids too. I spray insecticide about 12 or 13 times, plus herbicide once and growth regulator twice. It is exhausting work walking with the sprayer at my age, but cotton brings in more cash per mu than maize, so I keep those 3 mu. I hope for about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu. I do not try new things — last year was okay, so this year I do the same. Changing is risky, and I cannot afford a bad year.
